The words

Stricken, smitten, and afflicted,
See Him dying on the tree!
'Tis the Christ by man rejected;
Yes, my soul, 'tis He, 'tis He!
'Tis the long expected prophet,
David's Son, yet David's Lord;
Proofs I see sufficient of it:
'Tis a true and faithful Word.

Tell me, ye who hear Him groaning,
Was there ever grief like His?
Friends through fear His cause disowning,
Foes insulting his distress:
Many hands were raised to wound Him,
None would interpose to save;
But the deepest stroke that pierced Him
Was the stroke that Justice gave.

Ye who think of sin but lightly,
Nor suppose the evil great,
Here may view its nature rightly,
Here its guilt may estimate.
Mark the Sacrifice appointed!
See Who bears the awful load!
'Tis the Word, the Lord's Anointed,
Son of Man, and Son of God.

Here we have a firm foundation,
Here the refuge of the lost.
Christ the Rock of our salvation,
Christ the Name of which we boast.
Lamb of God for sinners wounded!
Sacrifice to cancel guilt!
None shall ever be confounded
Who on Him their hope have built.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum Bb and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on l, (G), on the first syllable of “Stricken”, as a pickup before the first full bar.
  • Count the time. 6/4 means six crotchet beats (two dotted minims) in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f l t and the chromatic se. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

The words are by Thomas Kelly, first published in 1804. The tune, O MEIN JESU, ICH MUSS STERBEN, is from Geistliches Volkslied, 1850. This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.

  • Words (1804): Thomas Kelly (1769–1855)
  • Melody (1850): From Geistliches Volkslied, 1850

Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune O MEIN JESU, ICH MUSS STERBEN (From Geistliches Volkslied, 1850); words by Thomas Kelly (1769–1855). Questions about Stricken, Smitten, and Afflicted

What is the doh of Stricken, Smitten, and Afflicted?

In this version, in G minor, doh is Bb. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Stricken, Smitten, and Afflicted start on?

It starts on l, (G in G minor), a pickup on the first syllable of “Stricken” before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to l,.

Is Stricken, Smitten, and Afflicted in the public domain?

Yes. Thomas Kelly died in 1855; the words were first published in 1804 and the music in 1850. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
